title: The 2027 Majors Calendar: Who Will Write History at Augusta, Oakmont, and Beyond?
summary: The four major championships define careers and separate the great from the merely excellent. We preview the 2027 major season and the players best positioned to add to their major tallies.
content:
Golf's major championships are where legacies are written. The regular tour events — the weekly PGA Tour and DP World Tour schedules, the LIV events, the countless tournaments that fill the season — matter for ranking points and prize money. But the Masters, the US Open, The Open Championship, and the PGA Championship are where the sport's history lives. When people remember a golfer's career in fifty years, they will count majors.

The 2027 major season arrives with the landscape more competitive — and more complicated — than it has been for years. The LIV split has mixed the competitive field without settling the question of who the best players in the world are. The ranking system remains contested. And a cluster of players in their late 20s and early 30s are reaching the peak of their abilities simultaneously.

The Masters — Augusta, April

Augusta National remains golf's cathedral. The azaleas, the par-3 course, the green jacket, the reverence with which the entire sport treats the first major of the year — the Masters occupies a position in golf that no other event in any sport quite replicates. The course's characteristics — the premium on accurate iron play, the importance of putting on some of the game's most demanding greens, the drama of Amen Corner — produce a Masters champion who had to earn it in ways that do not translate to other courses.

Rory McIlroy's continuing quest for the Career Grand Slam makes him the narrative focus every April until he either wins or retires. The story is not tiresome — it is one of sport's genuinely compelling ongoing dramas. At 37, the window is narrowing. Each Masters is now freighted with an urgency that earlier appearances did not carry.

The US Open — Oakmont, June

Oakmont Country Club in Pennsylvania is one of golf's most demanding venues. The rough grows thick enough to grip clubs. The greens are fast enough to make putting feel like an exercise in controlled falling. The US Open's traditional emphasis on par as a good score is amplified at Oakmont in ways that require a specific temperament: patience, precision, the ability to make bogey when a double is threatened and move on without letting it compound.

Historically, Oakmont rewards the best ball-strikers in the game — players who keep the ball in the fairway and hit greens with enough precision to avoid the most dangerous pin positions. The 2027 US Open will produce a champion who controlled a golf course that is designed to be uncontrollable.

Major championships reveal who you really are. The pressure, the history of the place, the knowledge that everything counts in a way it doesn't at a regular tour event — that changes players. It reveals the best and it reveals the limits. That is what makes them special.

The Open Championship — Royal Troon, July

Links golf is a different game from parkland golf. The wind shapes every decision. The ground game — using the turf to run the ball to the target — becomes as important as the air game. The bounce and roll of a links course cannot be fully predicted, which introduces an element of fortune that more controlled, parkland major venues avoid. The best Open champions have been players who embraced unpredictability rather than fighting it.

The PGA Championship — TBA, August

The PGA Championship is the fourth major and the one that most often surprises. Its status as the most recent of the four to be truly established at the elite level means its identity is less fixed than the others — less tied to a specific course, less associated with particular narrative traditions. It has also produced some of golf's greatest champions at some of their greatest moments.

Who Wins in 2027?

Prediction in golf is an exercise in humility. The sport has an almost unique capacity to produce winners who were not on anyone's list a week before they happened. What can be said with confidence is that the 2027 major season will produce at least one moment that redefines a career, one narrative that runs through the entire season, and one champion whose victory will be discussed for years.
